entries.name: Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP) Training Courses
entries.provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Singapore
entries.fields: Short courses for officials in public administration, economic development, urban planning, education, health, ICT, aviation and more
entries.eligibility: Government officials of developing partner countries (Cambodia is a long-standing partner) nominated by their agency; relevant job role; working English
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian officials are nominated through their ministries and the Cambodia-Singapore Cooperation Centre (CSCC) in Phnom Penh; the Singapore Embassy in Phnom Penh coordinates; over 17,700 Cambodian officials have trained under SCP.
entries.deadline_note: Rolling; each course on the SCP calendar has its own nomination deadline
entries.language_req: English

entries.name: ICCR Scholarships (General Scholarship Scheme and Mekong-Ganga Cooperation Scholarship Scheme)
entries.provider: Indian Council for Cultural Relations (ICCR), Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
entries.fields: Most fields except medicine/dentistry (engineering, IT, humanities, social sciences, business, agriculture, Buddhist studies, forensic science, arts, yoga)
covers: monthly stipend (approx. INR 18,000 UG / 20,000 PG / 22,000 PhD)
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizens aged 18–30 for undergraduate/postgraduate under the general scheme (up to 40 under the Mekong-Ganga scheme, higher for PhD); completed secondary school or bachelor's with good marks; English proficiency; medical fitness
entries.cambodia_note: Apply online on the ICCR A2A portal selecting the Embassy of India, Phnom Penh; the embassy Education Wing (edu.phnompenh@mea.gov.in, +855 23 210 912) screens candidates and administers an English test; Cambodia also has dedicated Mekong-Ganga Cooperation places; 41 Cambodians were selected for 2026–27.
entries.deadline_note: Opens around February and closes mid-April each year (2026–27: 15 April 2026); classes begin July–August
entries.language_req: English proficiency (embassy-administered test; some institutions ask for TOEFL/IELTS)

entries.name: Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme
entries.provider: Ministry of External Affairs, Government of India
entries.fields: About 400 short professional courses (IT, management, public administration, finance, agriculture, renewable energy, English, defence etc.) at 100+ Indian institutes
entries.eligibility: Working professionals and government officials of ITEC partner countries (Cambodia included), aged 25–45, at least 5 years' work experience, working knowledge of English, nominated/endorsed by employer
entries.cambodia_note: Apply online at itecgoi.in choosing the Embassy of India, Phnom Penh; the embassy vets applications and forwards them to MEA; the embassy holds ITEC briefings for Cambodian officials.
entries.deadline_note: Year-round; apply at least about 3 months before the course starts (course calendar runs April–March)
entries.language_req: working knowledge of English

entries.name: Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship to Foreign Students (BDGS)
entries.provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Brunei Darussalam
entries.fields: Diploma, undergraduate and master's programmes at UBD, UNISSA, UTB, KUPU SB and Politeknik Brunei
covers: accommodation at the institution's residential college
one return economy air ticket and baggage allowance
entries.eligibility: Citizens of ASEAN, Commonwealth, OIC and other countries (not Brunei permanent residents); studying in Brunei for the first time; not above 25 for diploma/undergraduate and 35 for master's on 1 July of the start year; meets institution's entry requirements; English proficiency (IELTS 6.0/TOEFL 550 for English-medium)
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is eligible as an ASEAN member; apply online on the MFA Brunei BDGS portal within the window; awardees are confirmed through the Brunei Embassy in Phnom Penh/Cambodian authorities.
entries.deadline_note: Opens around December–January and closes mid-February (2026/27: 15 February 2026); academic year starts July/August
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL 550 or equivalent for English-medium programmes

entries.name: Malaysian Technical Cooperation Programme (MTCP) Scholarship
entries.provider: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Malaysia
entries.fields: Most fields at Malaysian public universities, except medicine, nursing and clinical pharmacy
entries.eligibility: Citizens of MTCP recipient countries (Cambodia included); not more than 45 at application; Second Class Upper or minimum CGPA 3.0–3.5 at bachelor level (per current guidelines); IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 60 or English-medium degree; not concurrently on another scholarship; full-time master's at an approved Malaysian university
entries.cambodia_note: Apply online on the MTCP scholarship portal; no embassy nomination required, though the Malaysian Embassy in Phnom Penh may verify documents.
entries.deadline_note: Opens around April and closes in June (2026: 12 June 2026) for the September/October intake
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 60 (or English-medium prior degree)

entries.name: Malaysia International Scholarship (MIS)
entries.provider: Ministry of Higher Education, Malaysia
entries.fields: Priority areas: science and engineering, agriculture and fisheries, economics and Islamic finance, ICT, biotechnology, biosecurity and food safety, infrastructure and utility, environmental studies, health sciences (not medicine, nursing, pharmacy)
entries.eligibility: International students (Cambodians eligible); not above 40 for master's / 45 for PhD; CGPA 3.5 or equivalent; IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 92 (or equivalent); admission offer from a Malaysian university
entries.cambodia_note: Open to all nationalities including Cambodian; apply online on the MOHE biasiswa portal; no embassy step.
entries.deadline_note: Opens early March and closes early April (2026/27: 4 March–3 April 2026); shortlisted applicants interviewed afterwards
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL iBT 92 or equivalent

entries.name: KNB Scholarship (Kemitraan Negara Berkembang / Developing Countries Partnership)
entries.provider: Ministry of Higher Education, Science and Technology (Kemdiktisaintek), Republic of Indonesia
entries.fields: any of about 1,170 study programmes at 47 Indonesian universities
entries.eligibility: Citizens of developing countries with diplomatic relations with Indonesia (Cambodia eligible); maximum age 21 for bachelor's, 35 for master's, 40 for doctoral; required prior qualification; IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 53 (bachelor) or IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 61–71 (master/PhD) unless English-medium degree; recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy
entries.cambodia_note: Obtain a recommendation letter from the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh (submit passport, certificates, transcripts and university invitation letter), then apply online on the KNB portal.
entries.deadline_note: Opens early February and closes end of March (2026: 2 February–31 March 2026); results mid-June; departure August
entries.language_req: IELTS 5.5 (bachelor) or 6.0 (master/PhD) / TOEFL equivalents; Indonesian language year provided

entries.name: Darmasiswa Indonesian Scholarship
entries.provider: Ministry of Primary and Secondary Education, Republic of Indonesia (with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
entries.fields: One-year non-degree study of Indonesian language, arts and culture at about 54 universities
entries.eligibility: Foreign nationals from countries with diplomatic relations with Indonesia (Cambodia included); aged about 18–32 (window set each cycle); completed secondary education; able to communicate in English; good health; not a Darmasiswa/KNB alumnus or currently studying/working in Indonesia
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online on the Darmasiswa portal; the Indonesian Embassy in Phnom Penh interviews and endorses shortlisted applicants.
entries.deadline_note: Registration usually in the first half of the year (2026/27: 15 May–15 June 2026); programme starts late August/September
entries.language_req: basic English; courses taught in Indonesian

entries.name: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
entries.provider: Research Grants Council (RGC), Hong Kong SAR Government
entries.fields: any (full-time PhD at the eight UGC-funded universities)
covers: conference and research travel allowance HK$14,400 per year
support for up to 3 years (universities usually add tuition waivers/extra support)
entries.eligibility: New applicants to full-time PhD programmes at UGC-funded Hong Kong universities, any nationality; outstanding academic performance, research potential, communication and leadership
entries.cambodia_note: No country quota; Cambodians submit an initial application on the RGC HKPFS online system and full applications to up to two chosen universities by their own deadlines.
entries.deadline_note: Opens 1 September; initial application closes 1 December (12:00 noon HKT) each year for entry the following September (400 fellowships for 2027/28)
entries.language_req: English (IELTS/TOEFL per university)

entries.name: Macao Foundation Belt and Road Scholarship
entries.provider: Macao Foundation (Macao SAR Government)
entries.fields: any full-time programme at Macao higher-education institutions (University of Macau, MUST, Macao Polytechnic University, City University of Macau etc.)
covers: annual scholarship of MOP 60,000–80,000 towards tuition and living costs
entries.eligibility: Students from Bangladesh, Brazil, Cambodia, Hungary, Indonesia, Malaysia, Mongolia, Philippines, Portugal, Thailand or Vietnam, recommended by their home ministry of education or a PRC diplomatic post, and accepted and recommended by a Macao higher-education institution; about 20 places per year
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is named; obtain a recommendation from Cambodia's Ministry of Education, Youth and Sport (or via the Chinese Embassy in Phnom Penh) and apply through the Macao university's international office.
entries.deadline_note: Through the universities' admission cycles, generally spring for August entry
entries.language_req: English or Chinese per programme

entries.name: Kazakhstan Government Scholarship for Foreign Citizens
entries.provider: Ministry of Science and Higher Education of the Republic of Kazakhstan, administered by the Center for International Programs
entries.fields: any at 27 participating Kazakh universities (550 grants: 490 bachelor, 50 master, 10 PhD)
entries.eligibility: Foreign citizens of any country (Cambodians eligible), including ethnic Kazakhs without Kazakh citizenship; completed secondary/bachelor's/master's education; language of instruction Kazakh, Russian or English per programme
entries.cambodia_note: No embassy step; apply online at studyin.kz/admission during the annual window.
entries.deadline_note: Online window roughly late March to 31 May (2026: closed 31 May 2026); results in summer for September entry
entries.language_req: Kazakh, Russian or English depending on programme

entries.name: SEARCA Graduate Scholarship (Master's and PhD)
entries.provider: SEAMEO Southeast Asian Regional Center for Graduate Study and Research in Agriculture (SEARCA), hosted by the Philippines
entries.host_country: Various (Philippines, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesia partner universities)
entries.fields: Agriculture and related sciences (agri-food systems, rural development, natural resources, agricultural economics)
entries.eligibility: Nationals of SEAMEO member countries (Cambodia included); typically under 35 (MS) / under 40 (PhD); employed by a university, government agency or research institution in the home country; strong academic record; English proficiency
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply online through SEARCA's iSCHO portal with endorsement from their employer/ministry (e.g. Ministry of Agriculture or MoEYS); no embassy step.
entries.deadline_note: Call opens around June–July with deadline 30 September for the following academic year (AY2026–27 closed 30 September 2025)
entries.language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS per host university)

entries.name: JDS – Project for Human Resource Development Scholarship (Cambodia)
entries.provider: Government of Japan (JICA grant aid), implemented by JICE
entries.fields: Development-related English-taught programmes (public policy, economics, law, engineering, agriculture, education, ICT, health, environment)
entries.eligibility: Cambodian nationals aged about 22–39 (master's), university graduates working in the Cambodian government or designated organizations with around 2+ years' experience; doctoral track for officials/JDS alumni (older age cap); English-taught study
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia-specific programme managed by the JICE JDS Project Office in Phnom Penh; apply via the JDS Cambodia page, with document screening, English test and interviews; about 20–25 places a year.
entries.deadline_note: Call opens around September–October with deadline in late November (2026 intake: 28 November 2025, 3pm); results around March; departure August/September
entries.language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS per university, typically IELTS 5.5–6.0)

entries.name: KOICA Scholarship Program (Master's and Doctoral)
entries.provider: Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA), Government of the Republic of Korea
entries.fields: Development-related programmes (public policy, economic development, ICT, health, engineering, agriculture, education) at partner Korean universities
entries.eligibility: Government officials and public-sector employees of KOICA partner countries (Cambodia included), usually under 40 (master's) / 45 (doctoral), bachelor's degree, nominated by their ministry; English proficiency; not previously KOICA degree scholars
entries.cambodia_note: Apply through the KOICA Cambodia Office in Phnom Penh with nomination from the employing ministry/Cambodian government; programme-specific information sheets are issued with the annual guideline.
entries.deadline_note: Guideline published around June; applications close June–July (2027 programme: 29 June 2026, 4pm); study begins the following August/September
entries.language_req: English (TOEFL/IELTS may be required by the host university)

entries.name: Australia Awards Scholarships (Cambodia)
entries.provider: Australian Government, Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT)
entries.fields: All fields relevant to Cambodia's development (climate-related study strongly encouraged); general management degrees such as MBA are not funded
covers: pre-departure English language training in Cambodia
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen resident in Cambodia for the 24 months before the closing date; bachelor degree; at least 24 months of relevant full-time work experience at closing date; IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0 (or equivalent) at application; not an Australian citizen/permanent resident; women, people with disability and applicants from provinces encouraged
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is a priority country with its own Australia Awards Cambodia office in Phnom Penh. Apply online through DFAT's OASIS portal; the 2027 intake also allocated Mekong-Australia Partnership (AA-MAP) places to Cambodians under the same application.
entries.deadline_note: Opens 1 February and closes 30 April (14:00 AEST) each year; the 2027 intake ran 1 February–30 April 2026, and the 2028 intake is expected to open February 2027
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent TOEFL iBT/PTE) at time of application

entries.name: Australia Awards Mekong-Australia Partnership Scholarships (AA-MAP)
entries.provider: Australian Government DFAT – Mekong-Australia Partnership
entries.fields: Water security, climate action, gender equality/disability equity and social inclusion (GEDSI), combatting transnational crime, economic resilience and subregional integration
entries.eligibility: Citizens of Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Thailand or Vietnam meeting the standard Australia Awards criteria (bachelor degree, minimum work experience, IELTS 6.5 no band below 6.0, residency in home country); Master's by coursework or research in the MAP thematic areas
entries.cambodia_note: 30 AA-MAP scholarships across the Mekong subregion with 5 allocated to Cambodian citizens; Cambodians apply through the same OASIS application and Australia Awards Cambodia process as the main Australia Awards intake.
entries.deadline_note: Same window as Australia Awards: opens 1 February and closes 30 April each year (2027 intake closed 30 April 2026); 2028 intake expected February–April 2027
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.5 overall, no band below 6.0 (or equivalent)

entries.name: Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships
entries.provider: New Zealand Government – Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade (New Zealand Aid Programme)
entries.fields: Postgraduate study in subjects that contribute to Cambodia's development (e.g., agriculture, climate and renewable energy, disaster risk management, public sector management, education, health)
covers: home leave/reunion travel for long programmes
up to one year of English language training in Cambodia for preferred candidates
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen aged 18+, resident in Cambodia for at least 2 years before applying; at least 1 year full-time (or 2 years part-time) work experience; must not hold NZ/Australian citizenship or residence; must return to Cambodia for at least 2 years after study; Cambodians may only study at postgraduate level (Postgraduate Diploma, Master's, PhD)
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible Asian country (postgraduate only). Apply online at nzscholarships.govt.nz; the Manaaki New Zealand Scholarships Office in Cambodia is hosted by IDP Education at the ACE Tuol Tom Poung campus, Phnom Penh.
entries.deadline_note: One selection round per year, usually opening in February/March and closing in March; the 2026 round (for study from 2027) opened 1 March 2026 and closed 31 March (extended to 10 April) 2026; the next round is expected in February–March 2027
entries.language_req: IELTS 6.5 (no band below 6.0) or equivalent for postgraduate entry; English language training pathway available for Cambodian candidates

entries.name: Chevening Scholarships
entries.provider: UK Government – Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office
entries.fields: Any one-year taught master's degree at a UK university
covers: return economy airfare to the UK
travel grant to attend Chevening events in the UK
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen who will return to Cambodia for at least 2 years after the award; completed undergraduate degree enabling entry to a UK postgraduate programme; at least 2 years (2,800 hours) of work experience; apply to three eligible UK master's courses and hold an unconditional offer from one by 8 July 2027; not previously funded by a UK government scholarship
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia has its own Chevening country page and allocation; applications are made through the Chevening online application system and interviews are held with the British Embassy in Phnom Penh.
entries.deadline_note: Opens in early August and closes in early October each year; 2027/2028 applications close 6 October 2026 at 11:00 UTC
entries.language_req: No English test required at application; must meet the chosen UK university's English requirement (typically IELTS 6.5) for an unconditional offer

entries.name: Fulbright Foreign Student Program (Cambodia)
entries.provider: U.S. Department of State – administered by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh, Public Diplomacy Section
entries.fields: Most academic fields (clinical medicine and programmes requiring patient contact excluded)
covers: round-trip airfare to the United States
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen residing in Cambodia at time of application; bachelor's degree (for master's study) or master's degree (for doctoral study) with a strong academic record; minimum TOEFL iBT 88 / TOEFL ITP 570 / IELTS 7.0; relevant work experience preferred; not a U.S. citizen or permanent resident
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodians apply directly through the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh, which runs its own annual competition and online application; the 2027-2028 competition closed on 30 April 2026 (23:59 ET).
entries.deadline_note: Announced around February and closes 30 April each year; the 2027-2028 cycle closed 30 April 2026 and the 2028-2029 cycle is expected to open around February 2027
entries.language_req: TOEFL iBT 88 or IELTS 7.0 (or TOEFL ITP 570) minimum

entries.name: Hubert H. Humphrey Fellowship Program
entries.provider: U.S. Department of State (Fulbright program) – via U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh
entries.fields: Public policy-related fields: sustainable development, democratic institution building, education, public health, journalism, law and human rights, technology policy, etc.
entries.eligibility: Young or mid-career professionals with a completed undergraduate degree, at least five years of substantial full-time professional experience, demonstrated leadership and public-service commitment, limited or no prior experience in the United States, and English proficiency (TOEFL required for finalists). Ten-month non-degree program.
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodian candidates apply directly to the Public Diplomacy Section of the U.S. Embassy in Phnom Penh, which recruits and nominates Cambodian applicants each year. The 2027-2028 call closed on 19 July 2026 (23:59 Cambodia time); the next call (for 2028-2029) is expected in mid-2027.
entries.deadline_note: Announced in the second quarter each year; 2027-2028 cycle closed 19 July 2026. Next call expected around May-July 2027.
entries.language_req: English proficiency required; TOEFL (typically iBT 71+) or IELTS 6.0 for finalists

entries.name: Global Undergraduate Exchange Program (Global UGRAD)
entries.provider: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs – administered by World Learning
entries.fields: Any field (one semester of non-degree undergraduate study plus community service and professional development)
entries.eligibility: Cambodian citizen aged 18+ currently enrolled full-time in an undergraduate degree in Cambodia, having completed at least the first semester and with at least one full academic year remaining after the programme; demonstrated leadership; minimum TOEFL iBT 48 for finalists; not a U.S. citizen/permanent resident
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is an eligible country; applications are submitted through the World Learning online portal and screened by the U.S. Embassy Phnom Penh Public Affairs Section (PASExchanges@state.gov). The 2026-27 application has closed and the 2027-28 cycle had not yet been announced at time of research; confirm status with the embassy.
entries.deadline_note: Historically opens in November/December and closes in January/February for the following academic year; 2027-28 dates not yet published
entries.language_req: TOEFL iBT 48 minimum (finalists); good written and spoken English

entries.name: DAAD Development-Related Postgraduate Courses (EPOS)
entries.provider: DAAD – German Academic Exchange Service, funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ)
entries.fields: Development-related postgraduate courses: economics/business, development cooperation, engineering, mathematics, regional and urban planning, agriculture and forestry, natural and environmental sciences, medicine and public health, social sciences, education, law, media
covers: monthly payment of EUR 992 (postgraduate) or EUR 1,400 (doctoral)
health, accident and personal liability insurance
tuition-free study or fee coverage at the selected course
rent subsidy and family allowances where applicable
entries.eligibility: Nationals of developing countries on the DAAD list (Cambodia included); bachelor degree (usually four-year) in an appropriate subject normally not older than six years; at least two years of relevant professional experience after the first degree; willingness to return and contribute to home-country development; language proficiency required by the course
entries.cambodia_note: Cambodia is on the EPOS eligible country list. There is no embassy nomination: applicants apply directly to the German university course of their choice, which forwards its shortlist to DAAD.
entries.deadline_note: Deadlines are set by each course; most fall between August and October 2026 (some until December) for courses starting in 2027/2028 — see the DAAD EPOS deadline list
entries.language_req: English (typically IELTS 6.0 / TOEFL iBT 80+) or German depending on the course
